title: What happens when valid scopes disagree?
question: How should TurtleBlock resolve conflicting explicit initiative rules across project, branch, and purpose scopes without inventing a hidden priority hierarchy or allowing a narrower restoration to resurrect a broader revocation?
why_now: The new session-boundary authority contract requires exact same-scope carryover unless the learner explicitly restores initiative. That makes the next unresolved case visible: two valid learner-authored rules may overlap without an authored precedence relationship.
possible_possibles: Require an explicit human-authored precedence rule only when scopes actually conflict.
When two valid scopes disagree, choose less initiative until a human resolves the scope.
Make restoration strictly scope-local so restoring a branch never restores a project or retired purpose.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — what if the safest conflict resolver is to do less until a human names the scope that actually matters?
constraints: Do not infer a hidden scope hierarchy.
Do not let narrower restoration silently revive broader authority.
Preserve each directive and scope as separate provenance.
Conflict handling must remain reversible and human-governed.

ontology_mappings.rationale: Conflicting rules are still learner-authored boundaries and must remain consequential.
Precedence over participation rules should remain explicitly governed rather than silently machine-selected.
A remembered broader purpose must not pre-decide the conflict.
Persistent scoped state needs explicit conflict semantics.
A later human resolution should alter subsequent sessions without rewriting the original directives.
The human may reshape machine initiative when overlapping rules become visible.
Project, branch, purpose, restoration, and conflict resolution must remain distinguishable.

ctc_mappings.rationale: Learner-defined scope controls which purpose is foregrounded.
The unresolved conflict remains an open question rather than a machine-made default.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: Scope conflicts should be inspectable state.
Authority resolution is system governance, not automatic evidence of learning.
A learner can inspect and revise why a rule won or remained unresolved.
Priority rules encode power and should not be hidden.
Collaborative environments need explicit rules for overlapping participation boundaries.

uncaptured_residue.observation: A formal scope hierarchy may itself become an invisible machine-authored curriculum of authority.
The safest temporary resolution may be deliberate non-action rather than precedence.

wait_a_minute_connection.summary: TurtleAsk, cross-branch transfer, engine provenance, and session carryover all separate crossing a boundary from gaining new authority; overlapping scopes now test whether that rule survives collision.
wait_a_minute_connection.uncertainty: This may be a general engineering invariant or a family of local rules rather than a new ontology concept.
